ca_apron_the.blurb: A small roadside crag on the north side of Woodfords Canyon, along Carson Pass Highway in the Lake Tahoe region, easy to spot and only a couple of minutes from the car. The twelve routes are mostly trad crack and face lines, plus one aid line. Grades start around 5.7, with a good bunch at 5.8 and 5.9, a few at 5.10 and 5.11, and a single 5.12 for the strong. Rock quality swings from grainy to very good. Cracker Cliff lies right behind and to the north, and a large boulder to the west carries several problems. A handy quick stop for a short session.
ca_apron_the.parking_note: Leave the car in the little roadside pullout on the right-hand side, 3.5 miles up the highway from the Woodfords junction, directly under the rocks.
ca_apron_the.approach: A short walk of a couple of minutes up from the pullout; the crag stands just off the highway.

_expect.name: Bad Man Mezzanine/Lower and Upper Terraces

ca_bad_man_mezzanine_lower_and_upper_ter.blurb: A wall on the west side of Pinnacles National Park, near Hollister, built around a broad mid-height terrace topped by a big pine. Routes are one or two pitches, roughly 50 to 100 feet, a mix of bolted and trad lines. Most of the dozen climbs fall between 5.6 and 5.8, with one easier line and a couple of 5.9 to 5.10 options, so it suits newer leaders and moderate parties. Descent is by rappel from chained anchors on either the north or south side; the north rappel ends in poison oak, so go carefully.
ca_bad_man_mezzanine_lower_and_upper_ter.approach: From the west side parking lot, walk about 0.6 miles up the Balconies Trail to its junction with the Balconies Caves Trail. Then follow the marked climbers' path, signed with a carabiner symbol, up to the base. Stay on it, since the vegetation alongside is being restored.

ca_crystal_wall_area.blurb: A section of Slick Rock Dome in the Highway 50 corridor above Lake Tahoe, found just around the corner from the Slick Rock Slab sport wall beneath a large arch. Twelve face and crack routes, seven bolted and five trad, run from about 5.5 up to 5.10, with most of them between 5.7 and 5.9. Several are longer multi-pitch lines, and some older ones are runout in places, so expect committing moves. Coming down, take the easy walk-off over the dome's brow on the northwest side, or rappel from chains with 70 m ropes. It is a big open dome with little shade.

ca_asteroid_boulder_the.blurb: A large boulder in the Hidden Valley area of Joshua Tree National Park, east of the Manx Boulders in the Asteroid Belt circuit. It carries a dozen problems from very easy up to V10: four are VB, then a cluster between V2 and V4, with just two hard outliers at V7 and V10. The setting is sunny and exposed with little shade, and the circuit is quieter than Manx, leaning toward crack and seam climbing. An easy walk-off sits at the far left of the west face.
ca_asteroid_boulder_the.approach: From the Manx Boulders, follow the sandy wash east roughly half a kilometer to the Little Bighorn formation, then keep going about the same distance further to reach the boulder.

ca_deviate_wall.blurb: A small wall in the Limbo Area of Mission Gorge, inside San Diego's Mission Trails Regional Park. The short, steep, slippery approach passes a big stone staircase that is easy to overshoot. About a dozen climbs share the one formation, split between five bolted lines, four trad routes and three top-ropes, running from around 5.3 to 5.11 with the biggest cluster between 5.7 and 5.10. Landings below the lead routes are poor, so take care. A fair choice for a mixed-ability group that wants easy top-rope options beside moderate sport climbs.
